issues_detected.description: Release datasets under resources carry only identification fields and a description; keywords, creators, purposes, instances and variables are documented only at the undeclared collection level, which member datasets do not inherit.
issues_detected.recommendation: Declare the record as a Dataset (conforms_to_class) if the top-level series is the unit of interest, or copy per-release descriptive metadata into each resource.

issues_detected.description: File enumerations, formats, sizes and RO-Crate conformance are recorded in top-level file_collections and distribution_formats keyed by id fragments, not nested in the releases they describe.
issues_detected.recommendation: Nest each release's file_collections, distribution_formats, total bytes, conforms_to and access steps inside the corresponding resource.

issues_detected.description: No funders or creators are attached to any release; only the June 2026 citation string lists author names, without affiliations or grants.
issues_detected.recommendation: Attach creators with affiliations and the NIH award (1OT2OD032742-01, as listed by Dataverse) to each release.

issues_detected.description: Ethics, de-identification and population descriptors (Human Subjects: No, de-identified cell lines, donor descriptions of MDA-MB-468 and KOLF2.1J) are recorded only at collection level; releases name cell lines without donor characterization.
issues_detected.recommendation: Record human_subject_research, is_deidentified, ethical review and subpopulations on each release, or supply a caller context declaring human_subjects.

issues_detected.description: Each release has only a license string; IP holders, commercial-license negotiation, governance contact and intended/prohibited uses are collection-level only.
issues_detected.recommendation: Add license_and_use_terms, ip_restrictions and use guidance to each release.

issues_detected.description: Collection mechanisms, data collectors, processing pipelines and lineage are absent from the releases; descriptions only name data modalities, and provenance-graph files are not linked to their release.
issues_detected.recommendation: Attach collection, processing and derivation metadata (including the provenance-graph files) to each release.

issues_detected.description: Releases have versions and DOIs but no maintainers, update plan, errata or preservation commitment at resource level.
issues_detected.recommendation: Add maintainers and per-release errata/update notes.

issues_detected.description: Three releases have only a bare DOI; the June 2026 release adds a formal citation for the same DOI but no second distinct reference.
issues_detected.recommendation: Add formal citations to every release and link the CM4AI preprint as an external resource.

issues_detected.description: No known_biases at resource level; collection-level bias statements are brief and use no taxonomy.
issues_detected.recommendation: Document per-release biases (cell-line selection, protein-set overlap, embargoed data) with a standard taxonomy.

issues_detected.description: Version numbers are not monotonic across the series (October 2025 release 2.1, June 2026 release 2.0) and the March 2025 page shows Version 1.4 while its citation ends V1; these are per-DOI Dataverse versions, as the record's own caveat partly explains.
issues_detected.recommendation: State that version numbers are per-Dataverse-record and give a series-level release ordering.

issues_detected.description: The June 2026 release's caveat records a source conflict: the release page says 'Released on: June 17, 2025' while Dataverse gives 2026-06-17; the record uses the Dataverse date and discloses the conflict.
issues_detected.recommendation: None beyond retaining the disclosed caveat.

issues_detected.description: The June 2026 citation contains the author name 'Ballllosero Navarro F', which looks like a transcription error (possibly present in the source).
issues_detected.recommendation: Verify the author name against the Dataverse record.

issues_detected.description: The record's top-level description says it 'describes the CM4AI dataset as an ongoing series of data releases' but declares no class; with nonempty resources it is evaluated as a collection, so its extensive series-level documentation does not count toward any release.
issues_detected.recommendation: Declare conforms_to_class Dataset if the series is the dataset being documented.

semantic_insights: Scope: the input has no class wrapper or conforms_to_class and has four resources, so it is evaluated as a collection of four release datasets (#/resources/0-3); each item score is the minimum across releases and collection metadata is not inherited.

The undeclared top-level wrapper is richly documented (29 keywords, 48 affiliated creators, NIH funders, ethics reviewers, collection mechanisms, MuSIC pipeline, file enumerations with MD5 checksums), but none of it is attached to the scored release units; most deductions follow from that structure rather than from missing knowledge.
Each release has a well-formed 10.18130 DOI (University of Virginia Dataverse), a persistentId landing page, a version, Beta status and an issue date.
The record discloses source conflicts (release date, version label) in source_caveats rather than silently choosing a value.

correctness_validations.doi_format: valid (10.18130 prefix, University of Virginia Dataverse) for all four release DOIs
correctness_validations.grant_number_format: not_present at resource level (collection-level 1OT2OD032742-01, 3OT2OD032742-01S2 and 5U54HG012513-02 follow NIH patterns but are not inherited)
